lead.headline: OpenAI president says company will be ready to go public in 2027
lead.summary: OpenAI president Greg Brockman said at a Wall Street Journal tech conference that the company would be ready for a 2027 listing, Reuters reported. Asked on stage, he replied "I think so." He also said business customers now account for most of OpenAI's sales, but gave no figure for that share or for total revenue. OpenAI has not set a date for a listing.

main.headline: OpenAI pipeline finds 948 Linux kernel privilege-escalation vulnerabilities
main.summary: OpenAI says it built an autonomous pipeline that found, validated and generated patches for 948 local privilege-escalation vulnerabilities in the Linux kernel. The Hacker News reports the run took 30 hours. Gizmodo reports the pipeline racked up $1.2 million in API costs, and BigGo Finance gives $1.21 million. Outlets differ on the run's length: GBHackers News says 10 days.

main.headline: OpenAI to acquire developer tooling startup Pierre Computer
main.summary: OpenAI announced plans to acquire Pierre Computer Company, which runs a cloud service where AI agents store code. Terms were not disclosed, and The Decoder reports the deal still needs regulatory approval. Pierre's open-source libraries Trees and Diffs already power the interface of OpenAI's Codex coding tool. OpenAI says it will keep them open source and plans to integrate Pierre's paid code hosting features into Codex.

main.headline: ChatGPT adds animated GIF creation with Images 2.6 model
main.summary: ChatGPT can now create animated GIFs from a text prompt or an uploaded photo. Users can adjust animation speed and edit individual frames. The feature comes with OpenAI's new Images 2.6 model, which is rolling out to all ChatGPT and Codex users on web, desktop and mobile. OpenAI also launched API models GPT-Image-2.6 Flare and Sunburst, and says users generate over 4 billion images per week, up from 3 billion in September.

main.headline: Microsoft rejects option to expand Nscale's Texas data center deal
main.summary: Microsoft declined an option to more than double its Texas data center contract with Nscale, the Financial Times reports, citing sources. The option covered a second 700-megawatt phase at the Barstow site from late 2027. The existing Texas contract stays in place. Nscale is seeking a valuation of up to $35 billion in its New York IPO.
